Topic.label: The Concept and Notation of Angles

Question: Which of the following statements about angle notation is correct?

Choices.A: \(\angle AOB\) and \(\angle BOA\) represent two different angles.
Choices.B: \(\angle O\) can be used regardless of how many angles there are at the vertex.
Choices.C: \(\angle 1\) is an angle named using three uppercase letters.
Choices.D: In \(\angle AOB\), the middle letter O represents the vertex of the angle.

Solution: When an angle is named using three uppercase letters, the vertex letter is written in the middle, and \(\angle AOB\) and \(\angle BOA\) are the same angle. When there are multiple angles at a vertex, the vertex letter alone cannot be used to name an angle. \(\angle 1\) is an angle named using a number.
